knowledge.title_en: The Mortgage Spread: Why 7% Mortgages Sit on a 5% Treasury
knowledge.body_en:
A 30-year US mortgage rate is not set by the Fed. It is priced off the 10-year Treasury yield plus a spread that compensates investors in mortgage-backed securities for two risks: the borrower may refinance early when rates fall (prepayment risk), or hold on far longer when rates rise (extension risk). Lenders add their own margin on top.

The spread is not constant. It widens when rate volatility is high, when the Fed stops buying MBS, or when banks pull back from holding them. That is why mortgage rates can climb faster than Treasuries in a tightening cycle, and why a 7% mortgage can coexist with a 5% ten-year.
knowledge.why_en: With the 10-year near 4.97% and 30-year mortgages back above 7%, the spread itself is a live gauge of how nervous rate markets are.
